extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers interested in heroism, leadership, historical character-portraiture, and literary criticism (esp. of Cromwell)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for recognizing, portraying, or judging 'great men' and heroic leaders in history or creative writing, emphasizing inward qualities (vision, silence, prayer), practical action over eloquence, and the moral complexity of ambition and power.

rubrics_metrics.name: True Hero vs Sham-Hero (the King merely dressed in King-gear)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish a real Hero/Governor/Captain from the 'Sham-Hero' who only wears the outward trappings of authority: 'The Valet-World _has_ to be governed by the Sham-Hero, by the King merely _dressed_ in King-gear.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate authenticity by looking past ceremonial signs and titles to the substance of leadership: does the person genuinely embody governing virtues or merely perform them? Beware judging authority by ballot-boxes or outward figure alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophetic inwardness: 'Prophet who could not speak'
rubrics_metrics.description: A prophetic man may be 'inarticulate' yet possess deep vision and sympathy: 'Rude, confused, struggling to utter himself... visions of the Devil, nervous dreams... and yet such a clear determinate man's-energy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a heroic figure, value inner vision, passionate sympathy, and an often-chaotic interior life as signs of profundity rather than dismissing inarticulacy as weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellect as seeing and ascertaining, not mere eloquence
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellect is defined as 'seeing and ascertaining' rather than speaking or logicizing: 'Intellect is not speaking and logicizing; it is seeing and ascertaining.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not equate verbal fluency with intellectual strength; judge by the clarity and correctness of perception and decisiveness in action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue/hero-hood = Tugend: courage and the faculty to do
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue and hero-hood are fundamentally about capacity for action: 'Virtue, Virtues, manhood, _hero_hood ... _Tugend_ ... Courage and the Faculty to _do_.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess heroes by their practical courage and ability to effect change, not by rhetorical purity or formal moralism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity expressed in extempore warmth and depth (prayer/preaching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Warmth, depth, and sincerity in free outpouring (prayer, rhapsodic preaching) matter more than method: 'method is not required in them; warmth, depth, sincerity are all that is required.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In judging authenticity, prioritize spontaneous heartfelt expression (especially in spiritual or moral utterances) over polished form; these are signs of genuine conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on prayer and seeking higher guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Great enterprises are begun with prayer and the searching of the soul: 'All his great enterprises were commenced with prayer... they cried to God in their straits... till some definite resolution rose among them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the role of devout deliberation and moral/ spiritual consultation (literal or metaphorical) as evidence of a leader's conscientiousness and seriousness of purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reticence (prudent withholding) vs Hypocrisy
rubrics_metrics.description: Superior men necessarily have 'reticences' and may justly withhold parts of their mind: 'There is no use for any man's taking up his abode in a house built of glass... A man always is to be himself the judge how much of his mind he will show.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat discretion and selective disclosure as necessary leadership skills rather than moral failings; distinguish prudent secrecy from deliberate deceit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid teleological error: judge course and starting-point, not only end-goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not substitute the goal of a career for its course and starting-point; historians often misread a man's life by assuming a preformed program: 'substituting the _goal_ of their career for the course and starting-point of it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a life or character, reconstruct proximate motivations and unfolding choices rather than imposing retrospective purpose; seek the actual sequence of emergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish prurient ambition from noble/necessary ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: Two kinds of ambition exist: the petty craving for notice (blameworthy) and the legitimate urge to unfold one's nature and serve duty (laudable): 'The selfish wish to shine... poor and miserable' versus ambition as the duty 'to unfold your _self_.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether ambition seeks self-exhibition or the fitting realization of gifts for public good; the latter can be a moral obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silence as a mark of greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Great silent men—'the noble silent men'—are the salt of the earth; silence (inner depth, roots) is superior to mere outward show: 'The noble silent men... Silence, the great Empire of Silence: higher than the stars.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value understated, unpublicized depth in characters or leaders; avoid equating visibility with worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of a Chief/King-figure in movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Movements often require a single decisive 'Chief Man' or King to succeed: 'To see and dare, and decide; to be a fixed pillar in the welter of uncertainty;--a King among them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying or judging collective action, recognize the practical indispensability of decisive leadership—even if uncongenial to democratic ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical authority over constitutional/formal pedantry when Reality demands
rubrics_metrics.description: When institutions are inert or pedantic, a leader may legitimately act outside formula to preserve order and effect good: the choice between 'Anarchy or that' (Protectorship) and the dismissal of Rump Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate claims to authority against the facts on the ground; a formal absence of mandate is not automatically disqualifying if practical exigency requires decisive action—yet this remains morally fraught.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inarticulate or broken speech can contain authentic meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Rough, chaotic utterances may imprison a real speech and reveal a man's heart: 'they afforded the first glimpses I could ever get into the reality of this Cromwell... you will find a real _speech_ lying imprisoned in these broken rude tortuous utterances.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss broken, unpolished rhetoric as proof of shallowness; attend to intent, feeling, and what is actually meant beneath the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for human faults without declaring a man a hypocrite
rubrics_metrics.description: A great man may have many faults and insincerities yet remain essentially genuine: 'Insincerities, faults, very many faults daily and hourly... The Sun was dimmed many a time; but the Sun had not himself grown a Dimness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance moral critique with recognition of overall character and achievement; condemnable lapses do not necessarily nullify a person's essential heroism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess purposes by fitness for the place, not only by coveting of place
rubrics_metrics.description: To judge ambition one must consider the fitness of the man for the place he seeks: 'Not the coveting of the place alone, but the fitness of the man for the place withal: that is the question.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a leader's pursuit of office, weigh his capability and duty to occupy that role, not merely his desire for status.
